definition: Multilingual Prompting is a core concept in Prompt Engineering. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Multilingual Prompting is
theory.body: Multilingual Prompting describes the methods and patterns used within Prompt Engineering to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Multilingual Prompting is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Multilingual Prompting matters
theory.body: Without Multilingual Prompting, systems built with Prompt Engineering are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Multilingual Prompting works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Multilingual Prompting follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Multilingual Prompting.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Multilingual Prompting
theory.body: Multilingual Prompting offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
